issues.body:
Every route row injects a lambda, and the probe rows call `_repo_confirmed_private` directly, so the one line that JOINS them is only covered where a flow test drives `main()` with a private route.

That covers groom-mint (`_test_gh_flows` stubs `api repos/org/private`), metrics (`responses[("api", "repos/org/private")]`) and park-stock (`_test_route_wiring` fake_run). It does NOT cover ci-latency (`_alert_route` is called only at line 2553 in `main()` and in lambda-injected rows), dispatch-stall (its flow harness pops ALERT_REPO at line 1119), or triage.

Concretely: mutating line 928's default to `else (lambda r, t: True)` — the exact fail-open this PR exists to close — leaves ALL SIX files green, because the probe rows still pass and the route rows never consult the default. In the three files above the default expression is never evaluated at all, so even a misspelled callee would surface only in production.

This is narrower than round 1's finding (the helper's fail-closed branches are now fully pinned, and the always-FALSE direction is killed in the three files with flow coverage), and the binding is byte-identical to the audited reference — hence minor, not blocking. But the reference file does carry the killing row: groom-alert.py:358 drives the flow with `visibility='{"private": false}'` and asserts the fallback end to end.
issues.fix_hint: Add one end-to-end row per file in which the LIVE default probe returns a non-private payload and the route is asserted to fall back to the registry. In groom-mint/metrics/park-stock this is a one-line variant of the stub already added (return `{"private": false}` and assert `-R` is the registry with no ALERT_TOKEN in env), mirroring groom-alert.py:356-362. For ci-latency/dispatch-stall/triage, the cheapest equivalent is to call `_alert_route("org/private", "tok", "org/registry")` with NO injected lambda while `_gh` is still swapped for the probe fake, asserting `("org/private", "tok")` on the private stub and `("org/registry", None)` on the public one — that pins the default binding without needing a full main() harness.
issues.title: No test kills an always-true default: the `confirmed_private=None` -> `_repo_confirmed_private` binding is unexercised in ci-latency, dispatch-stall and triage

issues.body:
dispatch-stall, groom-mint, metrics, park-stock and triage all carry the semicolon-joined form (`calls.append((args, kwargs)); return type(...)()`, `_gh = response(rc, body); values.append(...)`, `finally: _gh = original`), no blank line before the nested `def response`, several lines past the ~100-column width the rest of these modules hold, and no docstring.

ci-latency-alert.py:941 has the SAME helper written out properly, with a docstring ("Exercise every fail-closed result of this module's live repository probe"). Since the stated intent of these copies is to be identical, the five compressed ones are the odd ones out.

No lint config or lint job exists in this repo (no setup.cfg/.flake8/pyproject.toml, no ruff/flake8 step in .github/workflows), so this does not break CI — it is readability only, in files whose whole value proposition is that a reviewer can read the authority surface at a glance.
issues.fix_hint: Reformat the five compressed copies to match scripts/ci-latency-alert.py:941-961 verbatim (blank line before the nested `def`, one statement per line, `finally:` on its own line, and the same one-line docstring), so the six copies really are identical and a future diff to one is visibly a diff to all.
issues.title: `_private_probe_rows` is written in a compressed style in five of six files, inconsistent with the sixth and with the surrounding module

issues.body:
`ambient()` (line 730) was `routed("api")[1]`; it now scans for the `/pulls?` call and returns `None` if none is found. The half-configured rows assert `routed("issue", "create") == (REGISTRY, ambient())`.

If the census read ever stopped being issued, `ambient()` would return `None`, and `routed("issue", "create")[1]` is also `None` whenever GH_TOKEN is unset in the harness environment (the registry fallback passes `token=None`, so `_gh` never sets it) — the row would pass on two absences rather than on a match.

In practice this is well contained: `main()` cannot reach `upsert` without `read_pulls`, and the earlier row at line 764-769 explicitly pins `api_cmd is not None`. The disambiguation itself is correct and necessary — without it the new `repos/{repo}` probe would be mistaken for the PR census read. Flagging only because the sibling `routed()` helper documents exactly this hazard ("a row whose command vanishes REDS instead of quietly comparing two absences") and `ambient()` no longer holds that property.
issues.fix_hint: Give `ambient()` the same fail-loud shape as `routed()`: return a distinct sentinel (or raise) when no `/pulls?` call was recorded, so a vanished census read reds the two fallback rows instead of satisfying them by mutual absence.
issues.title: `ambient()` now returns None when the census read is absent, which can make the two fallback rows compare two absences

verdict.summary:
Round 2 addresses every round-1 finding, and the residue is genuinely minor.

(1) MAJOR #1 (helper shipped with zero direct assertions) is FIXED in all six files. `_private_probe_rows()` monkeypatches the module-global `_gh`, drives the REAL `_repo_confirmed_private` through all five outcomes, and restores `_gh` in a `finally`. Each branch is exercised and each row is killable: rc=9 pins the returncode guard; `""`/`not-json` pins the ValueError guard; `private: false` pins the negative; `"true"`/`1`/`[]`/`"yes"` pins `is True` against a truthy `.get()` slip (`1 is True` is False in CPython). The sixth row pins the observed call as `(["api", "repos/org/private"], {"capture": True, "token": "route-token"})`, so both the GET-only shape and the ROUTE-token threading are asserted, not assumed.

(2) MAJOR #2 and #3 (governed prose pinned false) are FIXED. park-stock and triage update `canonical_route_doc` and the live docstring together; both flatten identically, so GUARD 1's equality holds. The new `anchor` ("Presence is configuration, not verification") occurs exactly once, keeping the dropped-clause non-vacuity row honest, and the replacement wording trips none of the 16 `phrasings`, so the census row still reports `[]` over a scan that demonstrably covers the router.

(3) MINOR #4 (four stale docstrings) and MINOR #5 (structural census) are FIXED. metrics' new `api_shapes` row correctly reads `(2, True, "repos/", False)` off the AST: `f"repos/{repo}"` is a JoinedStr whose `values[0]` is the Constant `repos/`, and an added element, a non-f-string path, or any `-X`/`--method`/`-f`/`--input` literal reds it. NIT #6 (`[OPUS-5]`) is migrated in triage.
